To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the radiation levels in critical LHC areas are lower than initially expected, the radiation spectra are dominated by neutrons and that a combination of mitigation actions is required to achieve a safe and reliable LHC operation.

-The radiation level in the critical Lhc areas is significantly reduced by the LHC shielding, -The radiation levels in the most critical areas are still above the present radiation sensitivity of LHC electronics, -The radiation monitoring has been improved significantly and the measured values are in good agreement with FLUKA simulations.
- The radiation levels in critical areas are well below the radiation hardness requirements of the LHC detector electronics.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the radiation hardness of the LHC electronics, the radiation monitoring and the radiation shielding of the LHC.
the radiation environment in the LHC, in particular in the areas of the LHC experiments and the LHC control room.
the radiation hardness of the LHC electronics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the LHC electronics is well protected against radiation induced damage.
all mitigation measures are effective in their purpose.
the LHC electronics is well protected and that no significant impact of radiation on the LHC operation is foreseen.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the radiation monitoring and mitigation actions performed during the 2013/2014 shutdown have been successfully applied, allowing to run the machine at the highest luminosity ever reached.

, although the radiation level in the critical areas is still well above the present electronics tolerance limits, the mitigation actions taken during the 2008 and 2009 shutdowns are already having a positive effect on the LHC operation.
we have a clear understanding of the radiation environment in all relevant areas and that we are well prepared to cope with the present radiation levels.
The main takeaway from our work is that
radiation levels in the present LHC areas have been reduced to a tolerable level.
the radiation levels in all critical areas are well below the radiation sensitivities of present LHC electronics.
radiation effects in LHC electronics will be manageable with present mitigation actions.
